html:
The TypeScript you write every day, with an example for each feature. Paste a JSON response into the JSON to TypeScript tool to get its types instantly.

Basic Types

let name: string = "Ada";
let age: number = 36;
let active: boolean = true;
let tags: string[] = ["ts", "js"];
let point: [number, number] = [3, 4]; // tuple
let anything: unknown = JSON.parse("{}"); // must be narrowed before use
let id: string | number = 42; // union
Type Use it for
unknown Values you know nothing about yet: safe, forces a check
any Turning type checking off; avoid
void Functions that return nothing
never Things that can't happen: a function that always throws
null, undefined Missing values, checked with strictNullChecks

Objects: Interface or Type

interface User {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  email?: string; // optional
  readonly createdAt: Date; // can't be reassigned
}

type Point = { x: number; y: number };
type Id = string | number; // only `type` can name a union
Feature interface type
Object shapes Yes Yes
Unions, tuples, primitives No Yes
extends another Yes With &
Merges duplicate declarations Yes No

Use either for objects; be consistent. Index signatures for dictionaries: { [key: string]: number } or Record<string, number>.

Functions

function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}

const greet = (name: string, greeting = "Hello"): string =>
  `${greeting}, ${name}`;

function log(message: string, ...values: unknown[]): void {}

type Handler = (event: MouseEvent) => void;

// Overloads
function parse(value: string): number;
function parse(value: number): string;
function parse(value: string | number) {
  return typeof value === "string" ? Number(value) : String(value);
}

Narrowing

function format(value: string | number | Date) {
  if (typeof value === "string") return value.toUpperCase();
  if (value instanceof Date) return value.toISOString();
  return value.toFixed(2); // number here
}

// Discriminated union: a shared literal field tells the cases apart
type Result =
  { status: "ok"; data: string } | { status: "error"; message: string };

function show(result: Result) {
  switch (result.status) {
    case "ok":
      return result.data;
    case "error":
      return result.message;
    default: {
      const unreachable: never = result; // errors if a case is missing
      return unreachable;
    }
  }
}

// Custom type guard
function isUser(value: unknown): value is User {
  return typeof value === "object" && value !== null && "id" in value;
}

Generics

function first<T>(items: T[]): T | undefined {
  return items[0];
}
first([1, 2, 3]); // number | undefined

function getProperty<T, K extends keyof T>(object: T, key: K): T[K] {
  return object[key];
}

interface ApiResponse<T = unknown> {
  data: T;
  error?: string;
}

extends constrains a type parameter; = unknown gives it a default.

Utility Types

Utility Result
Partial<User> Every property optional
Required<User> Every property required
Readonly<User> Every property readonly
Pick<User, "id" | "name"> Only those properties
Omit<User, "email"> Every property except those
Record<"a" | "b", number> An object with those keys and value type
Exclude<"a" | "b", "a"> "b": removes members from a union
Extract<T, U> Members of T assignable to U
NonNullable<T> T without null and undefined
ReturnType<typeof fn> What a function returns
Parameters<typeof fn> A tuple of a function's parameters
Awaited<Promise<User>> User: unwraps promises

keyof, typeof and Indexed Types

const config = { port: 8080, host: "localhost" };
type Config = typeof config; // { port: number; host: string }
type ConfigKey = keyof Config; // "port" | "host"
type Port = Config["port"]; // number

const roles = ["admin", "editor", "viewer"] as const;
type Role = (typeof roles)[number]; // "admin" | "editor" | "viewer"

as const keeps literal values and makes arrays readonly tuples.

Mapped and Conditional Types

// Mapped: transform every property
type Nullable<T> = { [K in keyof T]: T[K] | null };
type Getters<T> = {
  [K in keyof T as `get${Capitalize<string & K>}`]: () => T[K];
};

// Conditional: pick a type based on another
type IsString<T> = T extends string ? true : false;
type ElementType<T> = T extends (infer E)[] ? E : T;
type A = ElementType<number[]>; // number

Template Literal Types

type Size = "sm" | "md" | "lg";
type Side = "top" | "bottom";
type Spacing = `${Side}-${Size}`; // "top-sm" | "top-md" | ... 6 members

satisfies

const routes = {
  home: "/",
  blog: "/blog/",
} satisfies Record<string, string>;

routes.home; // still typed as its literal shape, but checked against Record

satisfies checks a value against a type without widening it, unlike const routes: Record<string, string>, which loses the exact keys.

Classes

class Account {
  private balance = 0;
  static count = 0;

  constructor(public readonly owner: string) {
    Account.count++;
  }

  deposit(amount: number): void {
    this.balance += amount;
  }
}

abstract class Shape {
  abstract area(): number;
}

class Circle extends Shape {
  constructor(private radius: number) {
    super();
  }
  area() {
    return Math.PI * this.radius ** 2;
  }
}

private is checked at compile time only; #balance is truly private at runtime.

Enums and Their Alternative

enum Direction {
  Up = "UP",
  Down = "DOWN",
}

// Often preferred: a union of literals, no runtime code
type Direction2 = "UP" | "DOWN";

Assertions

const input = document.querySelector("#email") as HTMLInputElement;
const user = maybeUser!; // non-null assertion: you promise it's not null

Assertions don't check anything at runtime: prefer narrowing when you can.

tsconfig Options Worth Knowing

Option Does
"strict": true Turns on all strict checks: always use it in new code
"noUncheckedIndexedAccess" array[i] is T | undefined, catching out-of-range bugs
"target" The JavaScript version to emit, like "ES2022"
"module" / "moduleResolution" How imports work: "NodeNext" for Node, "bundler" with Vite
"noEmit": true Only type check, let a bundler build
"paths" Import aliases like @/components
"skipLibCheck": true Skip checking .d.ts files in dependencies: faster
